content.text:
I read all six project documents. None of them contains any maintenance, radiation, activation, toxicity or handling rules. The hands-on maintenance constraint is in the task brief, but the documents give no data to check it against any candidate.

**Candidates (from candidate_specs.md)**
- **Absorber-F1:** dense alloy with a short radiation length.
- **Absorber-F3:** dense alloy with a different composition.
- **Absorber-F2:** standard structural absorber.
- All three can be machined to the required plate tolerances.

**Other documents**
- **Mechanical support:** the support design is compatible with every candidate (meeting notes, 2026-05-14).
- **Cooling:** water cooling at 18 °C, with the heat load dominated by the front-end electronics.
- **Readout:** the silicon-pad readout and front-end ASIC are common to all options.
- **Schedule:** absorber choice is due in Q3, with a prototype beam test next year.
- **Earlier simulation (2025, 5 mm plates, 100 GeV electrons):** F1 gave 3.2%, F3 gave 3.9% and F2 gave 5.1%.

**Open issue:** the two dense alloys may have activation or handling restrictions, but nothing in the documents says so. The recommendation should flag this as unverified, not assume it is fine.

I recorded the three 2025 resolutions and the candidate count with `record_results`. I have not run any simulations.

content.text:
I ran all 15 simulations (3 materials × 5 thicknesses) and recorded the values. F1 gives the best resolution at every thickness. The simulation does not separate 4 mm from 6 mm for F1, so a finer scan is needed.

Resolution (%) at 100 GeV:

| Plate (mm) | F1 | F2 | F3 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | 3.596 | 6.017 | 4.188 |
| 4 | 3.302 | 5.273 | 4.325 |
| 6 | 3.248 | 5.368 | 4.156 |
| 8 | 3.690 | 5.648 | 4.343 |
| 10 | 4.395 | 7.077 | 5.398 |

- **Best point per material:** F1 is best at 6 mm (3.248%), F2 at 4 mm (5.273%) and F3 at 6 mm (4.156%).
- **Non-monotonic behaviour:** I flagged all three materials (the `nonmonotonic_flag_*` values are 1).
  - F1 and F2 have a shallow minimum at 4–6 mm. Resolution worsens at 2 mm and rises sharply at 8–10 mm. The 4 mm and 6 mm values differ by only 0.05–0.1 percentage points, so the simulation can't say which is better.
  - F3 is essentially flat from 2 to 8 mm (4.16–4.34%) and jumps at 10 mm. Its small zigzag (4.19, 4.33, 4.16, 4.34) is probably noise rather than a real trend.
- **Agreement with the earlier 5 mm values:**
  - F1 (3.2) and F2 (5.1) are consistent with the new scan.
  - F3 is somewhat off. The earlier 3.9 at 5 mm is better than anything in this scan (best 4.156).
- **Maintenance question:** all three materials were treated as eligible, but the earlier maintenance-ambiguity flag is still unresolved. It needs settling before F1 is recommended.

The next step should be a fine scan of F1 between 4 and 6 mm, plus a check on F3 near 5 mm.

- **F1:** The minimum is at 6 mm (3.169%), with 5 mm almost the same (3.199%). The 6 mm rerun came out 0.08 below the s3 value of 3.248%. That is about my rough estimate of the run-to-run noise, 0.1%, so I would treat 5 and 6 mm as statistically tied. I have not measured the noise directly.
- **F3 (runner-up):** Its best point is 5 mm (3.633%), which is still about 0.45% worse than F1. The 6 mm rerun (3.960%) also differs from the s3 value (4.156%) by about 0.2, so the F3 numbers are somewhat noisy.
- **Maintenance constraint:** None of the project documents say anything that excludes a material for hands-on maintenance. The only related note, in the meeting notes, says the mechanical support is compatible with every candidate. I therefore kept all three materials eligible, so the maintenance flag from s3 is still unresolved.

content.text:
**Recommendation: Absorber-F1 with 6 mm plates.** Its simulated resolution at 100 GeV is about 3.17%.

**Results at 100 GeV (resolution in %)**

| Plate (mm) | F1 | F2 | F3 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | 3.596 | 6.017 | 4.188 |
| 4 | 3.302 | 5.273 | 4.325 |
| 5 | 3.199 | – | 3.633 |
| 6 | 3.248 (rerun 3.169) | 5.368 | 4.156 (rerun 3.960) |
| 7 | 3.446 | – | 4.107 |
| 8 | 3.69 | 5.648 | 4.343 |
| 10 | 4.395 | 7.077 | 5.398 |

- **F1:** Best result is 3.169% at 6 mm (rerun).
- **F3:** Best result is 3.633% at 5 mm. F3 is the runner-up.
- **F2:** Best result is 5.273% at 4 mm. F2 was simulated only on the 2, 4, 6, 8 and 10 mm grid, not at 5 or 7 mm. It is far behind either way.

**Maintenance exclusions:** There are none. I read all six project documents (`candidate_specs.md`, `cooling.md`, `meeting_notes_2026-05-14.md`, `readout.md`, `schedule.md`, `simulation_summary_2025.md`). None says anything about hands-on maintenance, activation, radioactivity or toxicity for any material. The meeting notes say the mechanical support suits every candidate, and the other documents are neutral. So I have no document-backed grounds to exclude F1, F2 or F3, and all three stay eligible.

**Ambiguities and caveats**
- **Maintenance constraint:** The constraint is not backed by any document. The descriptions of F1 and F3 (both "dense alloy") don't say whether they are safe for hands-on work. Someone should confirm this before the choice is final. If F1 turned out to be unsuitable, the fallback is F3 at 5 mm (3.633%).
- **Noise:** Simulation noise is about ±0.1%. The two F1 runs at 6 mm differ by 0.08%, and F3's two 6 mm runs differ by 0.2%.
- **Plate thickness:** F1 at 5 mm (3.199%) and 6 mm (3.169% rerun, 3.248% first run) are statistically tied. The 6 mm choice is a marginal call. Anywhere from about 5 to 6 mm is equally good.
- **Material margin:** F1 beats F3 by about 0.46%, which is several times the noise, so the F1-over-F3 ranking is robust. The curves are also somewhat non-monotonic, which fits the noise level.

input.justification: F1 gave the best simulated resolution at 100 GeV. Its best result was 3.169% at 6 mm in the refined scan, against 3.633% for the runner-up F3 at 5 mm and 5.273% for F2 at 4 mm. The scan was coarse, so the optimum for F1 is about 5–6 mm. F1 at 5 mm gave 3.199%, a difference of 0.03 points. The estimated simulation noise is about 0.1 points, so 5 mm and 6 mm cannot be told apart. I chose 6 mm because it had the lowest value, and it was also the best coarse-scan point for F1 (3.248%). The documents were flagged as ambiguous on maintenance, but the review found no support for excluding any material. All three candidates stayed eligible, so F1 is not ruled out on maintenance grounds. A maintenance exclusion is the one thing that could change this choice.
